items.p:
LESSON 1 — your Yiddish helps! Yiddish איך בין → German ich bin.
> Ich ___ Erik.
(I am Erik.)
items.why: sein (to be): ich bin, du bist, er/sie/es ist, wir sind, ihr seid, sie/Sie sind. Yiddish: איך בין, דו ביסט, ער איז.
Guten Morgen / Guten Tag / Guten Abend — the -en ending (accusative greeting). Yiddish dropped it.

items.p: Pronunciation: German w sounds like English…
items.why: German w = English v: Wasser, wir, Wein. (Yiddish ווּ / וואַסער — same sound.)

items.p: Which word means "the house"? (Yiddish: דאָס הויז)
items.why: Haus is neuter: das Haus. Three genders: der (m), die (f), das (n). Yiddish דער/די/דאָס works the same way!

items.p:
> Wie ___ du?
(What is your name? — literally: How are you called?)
items.why: heißen: ich heiße, du heißt, er heißt. ß = 'ss' sound.

items.p:
Careful: Yiddish ‘ער רעדט’ (he talks) — German uses a different verb for 'speak':
> Er ___ Deutsch.
items.why: sprechen (speak a language): ich spreche, du sprichst, er spricht (e → i stem change!). reden = talk/chat — exists in German too, but not for 'speaks German'.
